To fasten, to join to (literally and figuratively).

examples.text: You need to attach the carabiner to your harness.
An officer is attached to a certain regiment, company, or ship.
The shoulder blade is […] attached only to the muscles.
A huge stone, to which the cable on the left bank was attached, was removed years later

Turbines have been around for a long time—windmills and water wheels are early examples. The name comes from the Latin turbo, meaning vortex, and thus the defining property of a turbine is that a fluid or gas turns the blades of a rotor, which is attached to a shaft that can perform useful work.

glosses: To adhere; to be attached.

examples.text: The great interest which attaches to the mere knowledge of these facts cannot be doubted.

glosses: To include an attachment with a communication (especially an email or other electronic communication).

examples.text: I've attached the contract to this email.

glosses: To come into legal operation in connection with anything; to vest.

examples.text: Dower will attach.
it therefore becomes important to know at what time the lien for taxes will attach.

glosses: To win the heart of; to connect by ties of love or self-interest; to attract; to fasten or bind by moral influence; with to.

examples.text: incapable of attaching a sensible man
God […] by various ties attaches man to man.
attached to a friend; attaching others to us by wealth or flattery

glosses: To connect, in a figurative sense; to ascribe or attribute; to affix; with to.

examples.text: to attach great importance to a particular circumstance
To this treasure a curse is attached.

glosses: To take, seize, or lay hold of.

examples.text: Then homeward every man attach the hand / Of his fair mistress.

glosses: To arrest, seize.

examples.text: Eftsoones the Gard, which on his state did wait, / Attacht that faitor false, and bound him strait […]
Old lord, I cannot blame thee, / Who am myself attach'd with weariness / To th' dulling of my spirits: sit down, and rest.
